# Independent audit: one fine coordinate, sharp height sampling, and trapezoid mass



## 1. Arbitrary cosets, open caps, and the sharp constant

For any bounded interval with any combination of open and closed endpoints, including a singleton, the discrepancy between its length and h times the number of points of t+hZ is at most h. With k>=1 included grid points, its length lies between (k-1)h and (k+1)h; with no grid point, its length is at most h. The argument is independent of the coset offset.

For every closed or open halfspace, the within-fiber cap-volume function is measurable and its positive strict superlevels are convex bounded subsets of R, hence intervals with the allowed endpoint conventions. The open-halfspace proof does not require upper semicontinuity: Brunn--Minkowski for the bounded measurable sections gives the same convex superlevel property. The original compact body gives a uniform bound W on all cap-section volumes.

Integrating the interval discrepancy over 0<a<W gives exactly the stated absolute cap error hW. Tonelli includes each sampled boundary value in full because the integral of 1_(g(u)>a) is g(u). A single threshold equality has no effect on the integral. Zero continuous-normal caps, lower-dimensional bodies, singleton projections, and entire-source cuts are included.

The constant one is attained by the closed product [0,Nh] times K and by the vertical body {t} times K. Both have the extra sampled endpoint mass hW. These examples establish genuine sharpness for the allowed class; no boundary-null hypothesis was used.

## 2. Peak-to-total and affine normalization

Using a nearly maximal section and any point at each projection endpoint gives the two cone-profile lower bounds. Their integrals sum to L times that section volume divided by s+1, independently of the location of the peak. If the peak is at an endpoint, the other cone alone has the full length L. This proves

    LW/(s+1)<=A<=LW

even without assuming full dimension beforehand. L>0 and W>0 imply A>0. The endpoint cone attains the lower constant.

The relative cap error hW/A and the convenient normalized error 2eta/(1-eta) have the correct denominators. The latter requires eta<1 and is not claimed sharp. In particular divergence of L/h forces relative all-cap approximation independently of the continuous heights. The stated subsequence consequence for a failure of approximation follows by contraposition.

Under u'=au+c and x'=Tx+bu+d, the grid spacing and projection length acquire |a|, the peak section volume acquires |det T|, and total volume acquires |a det T|. Thus h/L and hW/A are invariant, with the actual affine lattice coset retained. The coarse-fiber summation includes zero-total-volume levels separately via the absolute bound.

## 3. Exact scope of the trapezoid identity

The hypothesis Q=conv(Q intersect (G times R)) is essential and is used exactly. It forces the projection endpoints to lie in G. The sampled lower endpoints form a convex sequence and the upper endpoints a concave sequence. Their piecewise-linear interpolants bound a convex region containing every sampled fiber, while each of its strips is the convex hull of two adjacent sampled fibers. Both inclusions establish exact equality with Q, not merely an inner approximation.

It follows that the width integral is exactly h(T-E), with E the average of the two endpoint widths. At a collapsed projection N=1, the same endpoint is counted twice in that average, so E=T and A=0. This handles a positive vertical segment correctly. For N>=2, summing the endpoint chord gives T>=NE and hence (1-1/N)T<=A/h<=T. The consequence T<=2A/h holds for every noncollapsed projection, including zero-width segments with T=A=0.

The sharpness statements have the correct scope: affine width sequences attain the lower inequality; zero endpoint widths give equality in the upper inequality. For N=2 the latter case may have zero mass, which causes no false positivity claim.

## 4. Concentration parameter and noncollapsed mass

At two coarse levels the actual hull has exactly the two endpoint slices. Summing the exact trapezoid formulas gives

    T=M/h+E_0+E_1,   E_0+E_1<=2w_*.

Thus w_*/T>=(1-M/(hT))_+/2. The same endpoint convention works when one or both coarse projections collapse. The parameter is M/(hT), not M/h alone.

Summing T_z<=2A_z/h over the noncollapsed levels gives T_nc<=2M/h. If exactly one collapsed level has positive sampled mass, it is a single fine fiber, so its mass is at least T-2M/h. There is no inference that small absolute M forces concentration if T also tends to zero, and no unsupported extension of the two-level allocation to arbitrarily many coarse levels.

## 5. Uniformly round opposite-slope example

For h=1/N and epsilon=h^2, each endpoint parallelogram has area 4epsilon and 2N+1 grid fibers of length 2epsilon. Thus

    M=8h^2, T=4epsilon(2N+1),
    w_*/T=1/[2(2N+1)], M/(hT)=2/(2+h).

Every defining vertex is sampled, so the full three-dimensional body is exactly the convex hull of its actual fine mixed set. The only coarse integer levels are 0 and 1. The absolute-area concentration claim fails as asserted, while the stronger relative concentration hypothesis fails to hold, since M/(hT) tends to one.

The contained tetrahedron has the four stated facet planes, normals of squared norm six, and slack one at (1/2,0,0). The fixed block map gives a unit inner ball. The outer box has centered squared radius 21/4; multiplication by six gives 126/4<36, proving the radius-six outer bound. Both lattice cosets and the continuous Jacobians are tracked correctly. The concentration ratios and asymptotics are invariant under that fixed map.

Finally the two distinct shears and height scalings turn the components into identical squares while keeping spacing h. This is only a componentwise discrepancy illustration. Each original component already has the absolute cap error divided by coarse mass equal to at most h/2, so the stated weaker bound h from the projection-length estimate is valid. No global common normalization or depth recovery is inferred from these separate maps.

All constants, endpoint conventions, and measure normalizations pass.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
